# Hosted API retention rule

Status: Support-facing interim rule (v1)  
Owner: Platform & Console — Ethan Park  
Last validated: 2026-08-01

## Supported guidance

- Hosted API-level logs are retained for 90 days by default.
- Longer log retention may be available as an add-on. Private deployments can instead forward logs to a customer SIEM; support must confirm the applicable order form and deployment configuration before promising either option.
- Treat configured region and runtime fallback as separate controls. Product acceptance criteria require fallback routing to produce an explicit audit event. This evidence does **not** establish that standard Hosted API data is region-locked or that fallback never crosses regions.
- For audit validation, collect the retention configuration, a representative log export, the retention-policy document, and retention-expiration alerts. The assurance memo is a draft evidence checklist, not a customer commitment.

## Unknowns — do not promise

Current evidence does not establish:

- retention periods for request or response payloads, embeddings, model artifacts, or aggregated metrics;
- deletion timing for active indexes, primary stores, caches, analytics copies, snapshots, or backups;
- timing after tenant termination or an erasure request;
- whether backups replicate across regions, their maximum retention, or whether an EU-only/US-only custody option covers backups;
- availability, format, or retention of deletion receipts, certificates, or customer-visible audit events;
- a default Hosted API storage country or a contractual residency guarantee.

Support must not translate the 90-day API-log statement into a purge SLA or a payload-retention promise.

## Validation before answering a questionnaire

1. Identify Hosted, Dedicated, or Private deployment and obtain the executed order form/DPA and any residency amendment.
2. Confirm the exact data class: API metadata, prompt/response payload, embedding, artifact, audit event, cache, analytic copy, or backup.
3. Ask Platform/SRE for the deployed retention configuration and expiration-job evidence.
4. Ask Security/Privacy for approved deletion, backup, residency, and attestation language.
5. For residency, verify both the primary region and every fallback/DR and backup path.
6. Escalate any requested deletion or residency SLA until a controlling policy or contract is cited.

## Evidence

- [Larkview HealthTech onboarding & risk handoff](/knowledge/company/sources/fireflies/customer-success/2026-04-02-larkview-healthtech-onboarding-risk-handoff.json) (`dsid_1ceb67c562a647838ca1b925f4187553`): Redwood states a 90-day default for hosted API-level logs; extended retention is an add-on, and Private can push logs to the customer SIEM. Transcript quality is marked medium.
- [Residency fallback pricing and launch acceptance criteria](/knowledge/company/sources/slack/product/1767123456-residency-fallback-pricing-and-launch-ask-negotiation.json) (`dsid_d9a15ab8f79c4c7e938f90cf3586da13`): fallback must be tested and explicitly audit-logged; it does not itself establish a residency promise.
- [Assurance micro memo: quick SOC 2 control probes](/knowledge/company/sources/google_drive/users/assurance-micro-memo-haruki-2026.json) (`dsid_c0a03597cb93476b9904666e1aedd6e0`): draft checklist for retention-control evidence and unresolved assurance questions.

arguments.summary: Support may state that Hosted API-level logs have a 90-day default and that extended retention may be available as an add-on; Private deployments may forward logs to a customer SIEM. No supported v1 evidence establishes payload, deletion, purge, backup, tenant-termination, or residency timelines, so support must validate deployment, data class, contracts, primary/fallback/DR paths, and retention-job evidence before committing.

arguments.content:
# Hosted API retention rule

Status: Support-facing canonical rule (corrected v3)  
Owner: Platform & Console — Ethan Park  
Last validated: 2026-08-01  
Replaces: interim v1 at this same path

## Customer-facing rule

Unless an executed enterprise contract, DPA, or residency addendum says otherwise:

- **Request/response payload logs:** retained 30 days by default. Enterprise contracts may configure 90 or 365 days.
- **Streaming and KV caches:** ephemeral; held in memory or short local caches for less than one hour unless the customer explicitly elects persistence.
- **Embeddings and derived vectors:** retained 14 days by default; a 7-day strict-ephemeral option is available. Longer storage applies only when the customer elects persistent vector storage under an SLA.
- **Model artifacts:** model snapshots and fine-tuned artifacts remain until explicitly deleted. Rolling backup snapshots have a 30-day default.
- **Verified erasure or tenant termination:** serving stops immediately and the tenant dataset is marked for purge. Primary data is purged within 30 days. Backups and replicated snapshots are scrubbed within 90 days. A deletion attestation/certificate is available after completion on request.
- **Backups:** backup retention is at most 90 days by default; longer retention requires agreement. Backups may replicate to a secondary region for disaster recovery according to the customer SLA.
- **EU-only custody:** available only with the hosted-enterprise data-residency addendum. For an EU-only contract, backups remain in-region and cross-region replication is disabled unless explicitly contracted.
- **Encryption and audit evidence:** cloud KMS protects data at rest by default. Enterprise customers may use customer-managed keys; HSM integration applies to Private deployments. Deletion and erasure events are retained in the audit trail for 365 days and may be surfaced in Console or exported for enterprise customers. Events include the actor, timestamp, object ID, and operation status.

Use “within 30 days” only for primary purge after a **verified** erasure request or tenant termination. Do not describe that as immediate physical deletion. Immediate action is cessation of serving and purge marking.

## Residency and cross-region caution

Hosted data is persisted in the tenancy's assigned primary region. Self-serve tenancy is assigned to a nearby regional cluster and is US by default for the cited questionnaire; support must check the actual tenant mapping rather than promise a country or cloud region from sign-up location alone.

Runtime fallback can route requests across regions when locality fails: incident SUP-7813 records EU-west traffic routed to US-east under the latency-fallback policy. Therefore region preference, primary storage region, runtime routing, DR replication, and backup custody are distinct. Only a controlling contract/addendum and deployed routing/backup configuration establish a residency promise.

## Remaining unknowns and limits

The evidence does not establish:

- deletion timing for customer-controlled or third-party vector stores;
- a generally available guarantee that worker/GPU-memory clearing can be retroactively proven after process termination;
- that every enterprise account has CMK/HSM, Console export, or a signed receipt without configuration or request;
- retention for aggregated or de-identified telemetry;
- a universal no-cross-region runtime-routing promise outside a controlling residency contract and verified configuration;
- whether a particular contract extends defaults.

## Validation before answering a questionnaire

1. Verify deployment mode and the executed order form, DPA, SLA, and residency addendum.
2. Name the data class precisely; never use “logs” without distinguishing payload logs, audit events, access logs, and aggregated telemetry.
3. Confirm the tenant's primary-region mapping, runtime fallback policy, DR target, and backup replication policy.
4. Confirm configured TTLs and recent expiration-job evidence.
5. Require a verified erasure/termination request before quoting the purge clock.
6. Coordinate deletion of third-party stores and request the deletion attestation only after the applicable purge completes.
7. For audit evidence, collect configuration, expiration alerts, event exports, deletion receipts where applicable, and KMS/CMK metadata.

## Authoritative evidence

- [Hosted API: Data geography, TTL & purge cadence — security questionnaire response](/knowledge/company/sources/gmail/aditya_rao/20260602-crestline-residency-ttl-playbook-response.json) (`dsid_7c0ce3505c1d46d8a00aa6680c35fbd3`): infrastructure-product-confirmed answers sent externally, covering data classes, erasure/termination, backups, EU-only custody, KMS, and audit retention.
- [Sanitization policy options and residency/retention for PHI — Q&A](/knowledge/company/sources/gmail/ben_carter/20250708-sanitization-policy-options-for-regulated-healthcare-qna.json) (`dsid_9d01b1a924fd4ee994233893b1096d8a`): Head of Security clarification on signed deletion receipts, cache eviction, embeddings, third-party stores, and evidence limits.
- [SUP-7813: EU requests routed to US-east during peering flap](/knowledge/company/sources/jira/customer-support/SUP-7813-eu-routing-peering-latency-fanout.json) (`dsid_a6242651cc144f53bc7fe653dddfc8de`): production evidence that runtime fallback can cross regions.

# Hosted API retention evidence matrix — correction working draft

Status: Unindexed working paper; exclude from promotion.

| Topic | Evidence / interpretation | Disposition |
|---|---|---|
| “API-level logs” default | Larkview call says 90 days; medium transcription quality and no data-class definition. | Reject as the canonical default. It conflates payload logs, audit logs, and possibly access logs. Keep 90 days only as an enterprise-configurable payload-log term. |
| Request/response payloads | Crestline response, confirmed by Director of Infrastructure Product and sent externally: 30 days default, 90/365 by enterprise contract. | Accept. |
| Audit events | Crestline: deletion/erasure audit events retained 365 days. | Accept; do not apply 365 days to payloads. |
| Tenant termination / erasure | Internal draft says “typical” primary purge within 30 days; final external answer says primary purge within 30 days after verified request/termination, backup scrub within 90 days. | Use the final external answer, while stating verification starts the clock and immediate action is serving stop/purge marking. |
| Backups | Crestline: maximum default retention 90 days; may replicate for DR; EU-only contracts keep backups in-region and disable cross-region replication unless contracted. | Accept, contract-dependent. |
| EU/region behavior | Product acceptance thread says fallback is audit-logged; SUP-7813 proves EU-west requests can fall back to US-east. | Reject inference that primary-region selection alone prevents cross-region serving. |
| Signed deletion evidence | Crestline offers attestation after completion; Security offers signed receipts for persisted storage objects. | Accept as available on request; do not promise retroactive proof for terminated worker/GPU memory. |
| Third-party vector stores | Security says deletion requires coordination outside Redwood. | Retain as explicit limitation. |
| Draft assurance memo | Lists evidence to collect but is marked draft and contains unresolved questions. | Use only as a validation checklist, not as a customer promise. |

arguments.summary: Canonical Hosted API support rule: request/response payload logs default to 30 days (90/365 only by enterprise contract); embeddings default to 14 days with a 7-day option; caches are ephemeral under one hour unless persisted; model artifacts remain until deleted and rolling snapshots default to 30 days. After verified erasure or tenant termination, serving stops immediately, primary data is purged within 30 days, and backups/replicated snapshots within 90 days, with attestation available after completion. Backups may replicate for DR; EU-only backup custody requires the hosted-enterprise residency addendum. Deletion/erasure audit events retain for 365 days. Region assignment does not itself prevent cross-region runtime fallback.
arguments.title: Hosted API retention support rule corrected v3
